facts: multi-cloud · multi-region · HA built-in · data-localization boundaries
~500 apps on K8s across 1,000+ namespaces — the platform IS this composition
20M+ policy-as-code checks/day gating IaC and deploys
Kafka cumulative pipeline 10B+ events/day ACROSS those apps; backlog peaks in the tens of millions on the largest
etcd fleets riding their size ceiling with autoscale relief — constant pressure-and-release equilibrium
100M+ active users; AI/LLM services in the customer-serving path
platform_context.note: Scale here means COMPOSITION — hundreds of apps × a thousand-plus namespaces × regions — not one big number. The platform runs tight: horizontal + vertical autoscaling releases pressure as fast as it builds, which means split-brain risk and single-points-of-failure stay HIDDEN under the complexity until an incident surfaces them. That masked class is what the observatory's blind-spot (ghost) node represents.

source_note: Input is a seeded scenario simulator (simulator/event_generator.py). Scenario provenance is split at the honest granularity: the failure-mode TOPOLOGY is source_derived from public reporting, but the specific numeric SHAPE PARAMETERS (degradation depth, phase timing) are operator_calibrated — tuned, not from any cited source. The spreadsheet-vs-signal response-time gap is likewise operator_calibrated ILLUSTRATION (labelled per value), not measured telemetry. Peaks + counts are COUNTED over the seeded event stream (peak_error_rate saturates at an operator-set ceiling; peak_latency_ms is the end-to-end queue delay, backlog / drain rate, and agrees with lag_seconds_of_flow). Incident-phase tags (build_up/cascade/recovery) and phase_counts are DERIVED by a trajectory heuristic over the stream (single-dominant-peak; a multi-peak real trace could mis-tag a later surge), not raw event fields. Each scenario maps to a canonical hub KRI via packages/kri-taxonomy. Reproducible under (seed, as_of).
